questions.q: Why can't a GlideAjax callback's result be used directly in a return statement at the end of onSubmit?
options: The callback is asynchronous and runs later, after onSubmit has already returned
onSubmit scripts are not allowed to use variables
The callback runs before onSubmit even starts
GlideAjax cannot be called from onSubmit at all
questions.explain: Asynchronous means the callback fires once the server responds, which is always after the triggering function has already returned.

options: addParam cannot be called more than once
GlideAjax does not support the getXMLAnswer method
return !isBlocked executes before the callback runs, so isBlocked is always still its initial value
Nothing is wrong - this correctly blocks the save when needed
questions.explain: By the time the return statement runs, the server hasn't responded yet, so the callback's reassignment of isBlocked hasn't happened.

questions.q: In the correct async-safe pattern, why does the onSubmit script call g_form.submit() inside the GlideAjax callback?
options: To programmatically re-trigger the form's submit once the server has confirmed the data is valid
submit() is required before addParam() can be called
To reload the entire page from scratch
To cancel the save permanently
questions.explain: Once the callback confirms the value is valid, it marks a flag and calls g_form.submit() to re-run the submit logic, which now passes the guard check.

questions.q: Why is getXMLWait() discouraged even though it looks like a simple fix for the timing problem?
options: It silently ignores the server's response
It only works inside onLoad scripts
It blocks and freezes the browser's UI thread while waiting for the server to respond
It is not actually part of the GlideAjax API
questions.explain: getXMLWait() is synchronous - it waits for the response, but while it waits, the whole tab becomes unresponsive to the user.

questions.q: In the working onSubmit pattern, why does the function return false even on the very first call, before the server has answered?
options: To block that initial submit attempt, since the real answer isn't known yet - the actual save happens later via g_form.submit() in the callback
Because GlideAjax requires the form to be closed before it can run
Because onSubmit scripts must always return false
To immediately cancel the GlideAjax call
questions.explain: The first return false buys time for the async call to complete; the callback decides, later, whether to actually submit.
